hook.line: Don Hernando is sure he told Tomás about the rent. When Tomás asks again, Hernando does not just say yes. He says it with a little offence, and Spanish has a few phrases built for exactly that.
hook.es: Pues claro que te lo dije.

examples.es:
¿Le diste la dirección?
Pues claro que se la di.
examples.en:
Did you give him the address?
Of course I gave it to him.

examples.es: Te juro que no fui yo.
Le aseguro que le devolvió hasta el último peso.
examples.en: I assure you he paid back every last peso. (formal)

Are you coming tomorrow?
Of course.

examples.es:
¿Ya cerraste la caja?
Pues claro que la cerré.
examples.en:
Did you close the till yet?
Of course I closed it.

examples.es: Te juro que lo voy a hacer hoy.
examples.en: I swear I'm going to do it today.

rule:
When someone doubts you, one word is not enough. Spanish repeats the verb and adds *que*.

*Pues claro que + verb*: of course I did. Repeat what was asked: *¿Lo cerraste? Pues claro que lo cerré.* It can sound a bit offended, which is the point.
*Por supuesto que sí / no*: of course (not). Calmer.
*Te juro que…*: I swear that…, with friends.
*Le aseguro que…*: I assure you that…, to someone you address as *usted*.

The sentence after *que* is a normal one, with the pronouns it needs.
smallPrint: Teachers call this *refuerzo de la aserción*: you reinforce a statement that someone questioned.

options: I don't know if I did it.

readAndPick.es: Te juro que no fui yo.
Le aseguro que llegamos a tiempo.
options: I assure you we arrived on time (to a friend).
I assure you we arrived on time (formal).
He assures us we arrived on time.

readAndPick.es:
¿Se lo dijiste?
Pues claro que se lo dije.
Te juro que voy a venir.
options: I swear I'm going to come.

readAndPick.es: Pues claro que vamos a ir.
options: Of course we're going to go.
Of course they're going to go.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (a friend asks: did you close the till? Answer: of course I closed it): Pues claro que ___ cerré. (la / lo)
accept: Pues claro que sí, la cerré.
yourTurn.why: *La caja* is feminine, so the pronoun is *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to a friend): I swear it wasn't me.
yourTurn.answer: Te juro que no fui yo.
accept: Te juro que yo no fui.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (formal, to a customer): I assure you we are open.
Answer a friend who asks if you're coming tomorrow, calmly saying of course:
yourTurn.why: *Por supuesto que sí* confirms without sounding offended.

yourTurn.prompt: Answer: ¿Le diste la dirección? Say of course you gave it to him.
yourTurn.answer: Pues claro que se la di.
accept: Pues claro que se la di a él.
yourTurn.why: *Le* plus *la* becomes *se la*, and the verb repeats in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a promise (to a friend): Voy a llamar a Vale.
yourTurn.answer: Te juro que voy a llamar a Vale.
accept: Te juro que llamo a Vale.
yourTurn.why: *Te juro que* goes in front and the rest stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Of course not.

pitfalls.why: To sound mildly offended, add *pues* and repeat the verb without *sí*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te aseguro que no fui yo, señor.
pitfalls.right: Le aseguro que no fui yo, señor.
Pues claro que se la di.
pitfalls.why: When you give something to him or her, *le la* becomes *se la*.

personal: Think of someone who doubts you. Answer them with *pues claro que* and the verb they asked about.
